title: "Session 9 · Positron and AI-assisted coding"
subtitle: "AI-assisted coding with GitHub Copilot as a worked example"
---

## Learning goals

Navigate an R project in Positron, distinguish the IDE from AI coding assistance,
and distinguish models, applications, context, tools, and execution environments.
Separate inline completion from four levels of explicit requests to AI.
Use GitHub Copilot as an example provider and Posit Assistant for chat and tools.
Verify the statistical meaning of suggested code and disclose AI assistance.
Copilot is optional. The same course rules apply to other AI tools.

The AI lesson follows four parts:

1. **Understand:** LLMs, coding applications, context, and the five interactions.
2. **Set up:** an example provider, modes, and permissions in Positron.
3. **Work:** predictions and four levels of explicit requests using the Session 4 SBP data.
4. **Verify:** inspect a week-12 SBP summary, repair its denominator, and check independently.

The distinction between a model request constructed by the application and an
explicit task request from the user connects the examples. The same synthetic
dataset continues from plotting and planning into statistical verification.

## Before class

### What is Positron?

Positron is an integrated development environment (IDE) from Posit, the company
behind RStudio. It gives you a place to edit code, run R or Python, and inspect
results. **R is still the language and interpreter that execute your R code.**
Positron uses an installed copy of R, so keep your existing R installation.

Your R syntax and source files carry over. In Positron, the Editor corresponds
to RStudio's Source pane, Variables to Environment, and Explorer to Files.
The slides include annotated screenshots and a complete panel comparison.
Positron opens a folder as a workspace and builds on **Code OSS**, the open-source
core of VS Code. This connects it to a broad developer ecosystem of AI and
advanced development tools. Keep your `.Rproj` file for use in RStudio.

Many VS Code extensions work in Positron, but Microsoft restricts direct use of
its Marketplace. Use Positron's Extensions view, whose default gallery serves
the [Open VSX catalog](https://open-vsx.org/) through Posit Public Package Manager.
An extension's license and technical requirements still determine whether it can
run in Positron. See the [extension guide](https://positron.posit.co/extensions.html).

Read more in Posit's [R guide](https://positron.posit.co/guide-r.html) and
[RStudio migration guide](https://positron.posit.co/migrate-rstudio.html).

### Install Positron

1. Download [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/download.html) for your computer.
   On a Mac, choose **Apple Silicon** or **Intel** to match your processor.
2. Open the download and follow the installation prompts. On macOS, drag
   Positron into **Applications**.

Keep your existing R and RStudio installations. We will introduce Positron and
connect Copilot together in class.

### Apply for GitHub student benefits

1. Sign in with the GitHub account you use for BIOS6301. Add and verify your
   student email in [GitHub email settings](https://github.com/settings/emails).
2. Open [Education benefits](https://github.com/settings/education/benefits),
   select **Start an application**, and apply as a student. Provide your school
   information and any requested proof of current enrollment, such as a class
   schedule or dated student ID.
3. After approval, return to Education benefits and follow the prompts to
   activate the free **Copilot Student** benefit.

See [GitHub's student application guide](https://docs.github.com/en/education/about-github-education/github-education-for-students/apply-to-github-education-as-a-student)
for application details.
